newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Man Yue Int'l ends debut higher.
newsitem.headline: HK's Man Yue Int'l ends debut higher.

text.p: Shares of electronic component maker and distributor Man Yue International Holdings Ltd bucked weak market sentiment to end higher on its first day of trading.
"The recent strong performance of some new listings aided sentiment," said Henri Lui, analyst at Mansion House Research.
The share closed at HK$1.23, HK$0.15 or 13.89 percent above the issue price of HK$1.08.
"It performed satisfactorily because investors who subscribed to the stock could make a profit," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.
The share traded in a range between HK$1.18 and HK$1.36. Volume was 38.33 million shares worth HK$48.78 million.
Man Yue makes and sells capacitors and resistors which mainly are used in consumer electronics products.
The company issued 55 million new shares at HK$1.08 each in an initial public offering which was 10.2 times subscribed.
Despite its encouraging performance, brokers said they expected the shares to dive down later on the diminishing of the trading interest on the stock.
There were concerns about the low profit margins of the business due to fierce competition in the electronics industry, analysts said.

Brokers also said they had feared investors, satiated with new issues which offered more attractive long-term prospects, such as China growth and China-based asset injection strategies, would find the issue unexciting.
